admin.unavailable: The admin helper is not running: lord-server must start with sudo and the user must be in the sudo group.
browserTabs.chromiumOpen: Chromium is open: its profiles change as soon as you quit it.
browserTabs.done: Done. The browsers use it the next time they open.

browserTabs.failed.one: {count} browser profile could not be changed and was left as it was.
browserTabs.failed.other: {count} browser profiles could not be changed and were left as they were.

browserTabs.firefoxKept: A Firefox profile sets this in its own user.js file, so it was left alone.
browserTabs.hint: On: Chromium and Firefox draw a single bar with their tabs and LordOS's window buttons. Off: they use the LordOS frame. It changes your browser profiles and applies the next time each browser opens.
browserTabs.label: Browsers: tabs in the title bar

browserTabs.othersOff.one: {count} Chromium profile still uses the LordOS frame
browserTabs.othersOff.other: {count} Chromium profiles still use the LordOS frame

browserTabs.othersOn.one: {count} Chromium profile still draws its own bar
browserTabs.othersOn.other: {count} Chromium profiles still draw their own bar

clipboard.historyHint: ❖V opens the quick panel and ❖⇧V the full one, with filters and preview.
clipboard.ignoreHint: By id (the Wayland app_id, e.g. org.example.PasswordManager). What these apps copy can be pasted but is not kept in the history.
clipboard.maxMBHint: When exceeded, the oldest images are deleted (not pinned ones).
clipboard.privacy: Never saved: what is copied from a LordOS password field, and what an app marks as secret (password managers do).
clipboard.saveHint: What you copy (text and images) is saved in your home folder and survives a restart. Off: memory only.
dock.autohide: Automatically hide and show the Dock
dock.autohideHint: It appears when the pointer reaches the edge of the screen; windows use all the space.
dock.magnifyHint: Icons grow when the pointer passes over them.
dock.recentsHint: The last three apps used that aren't pinned, after a divider.
dock.resetAsk: Reset the Dock to its defaults?
dock.resetDetail: The apps you added and the order you chose will be replaced by the theme’s. Open apps stay open.
dock.resetHint: Puts the theme’s apps back in their original order. Files stays first and the Trash last; Files, Settings and Apps can’t be removed.
dock.resetHintTaskbar: Puts the theme’s apps back on the taskbar in their original order. Files stays first and the Trash last; Files and Settings can’t be unpinned.
dock.sidesHint: Left and right are sides of the screen: they don't swap in a right-to-left language.
dock.taskbarHint: Lord Classic theme. Maximized windows don't go under the taskbar.
effectsHint: Turning off blur speeds up the desktop on slow computers.
firmware.hint: The bootloader lives in a chip on the board and starts it before the system. New versions come with system updates (the rpi-eeprom package); installing one takes effect at the next restart. Don't unplug the power while the board restarts.
firmware.missing: The bootloader tools are not installed
firmware.missingHint: LordOS updates the bootloader with the rpi-eeprom package, from the LordOS repository.
firmware.needAdmin: Only an administrator can update the bootloader.
firmware.pendingHint: The new bootloader is installed when the board restarts. Keep the power connected until the desktop is back.
firmware.pendingHow: The new bootloader is installed when the board restarts: log out and choose Restart on the login screen. Keep the power connected until it is back.
firmware.updatingHint: Preparing the new bootloader. This can take up to a minute.
general.name: Name
ime.hint: Type Korean, Japanese and Chinese with the Latin keyboard. ❖⌥Space switches between layouts and methods.
ime.noDict: This method's dictionary is missing: install the Debian packages for its language (Language & Region).
ime.title: Input methods
kb.hint: Every XKB layout (as in GNOME and KDE). With more than one, the menu bar button switches between them.
kb.noxkb: No XKB data (xkb-data package): only latam and us are available.
kb.testHint: Type here: ñ, accents (´ + vowel), ç, AltGr…

lang.hint: Interface text. Applies instantly; open windows and terminals are kept.
lang.title: LordOS language
pack.hint: Manuals, dictionaries and fonts for the language (manpages, hunspell, Noto…). Needs a connection.
pack.title: Debian language packages
reduceMotionHint: Stops decorative animations, like the spinning fan in Cooling.
region.hint: Dates, times and numbers, and the language of Linux programs (LANG) in new terminals.
region.title: Region (formats and programs)
scrollBarsHint: Automatically: a thin bar appears at the edge while you scroll or point near it. When scrolling: only while you scroll. Always: it stays visible.
session.browsersHint: Chromium and Firefox continue where they left off. Applies to every user of this computer.
session.hint: Leaves LordOS and returns to the console.
session.hintManaged: Ends your session and returns to the login screen. Open apps close, and come back next time unless reopening is off.
session.restore: Reopen windows when you log in
session.restoreHint: Apps open when you log out, restart or shut down come back with their windows in place. After a power cut or a crash LordOS asks first.
sharing.allowEmpty: The list is empty: nobody can connect.
sharing.allowlistFooter: Addresses and networks that may connect when "Only these addresses" is chosen. They still get blocked after 3 failed sign-ins.
sharing.badAddress: Write an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a network such as 192.168.1.0/24 (at least /8; IPv6 at least /16).
sharing.blockedFooter: An address is blocked after 3 failed sign-ins: for 15 minutes, then 1 hour, then 24 hours if it happens again within a day. You get a notification when it happens.
sharing.blocklistFooter: Always refused, before anything else, until you remove them.
sharing.fingerprint: Certificate fingerprint (compare it with the one your browser shows):
sharing.netAnyHint: Any address that can reach this computer, including the internet if a port is forwarded to it.
sharing.netAnyWarn: Connections from any address are allowed. Failed sign-ins still block the address, but a VPN is the safer way to reach this computer from the internet.
sharing.netLanHint: Private and link-local addresses of your network, and connections that arrive over a VPN of this computer. Public internet addresses are refused.
sharing.netListHint: Only the addresses and networks in this list can open the sign-in page.
sharing.noLan: This computer has no IPv4 address on the local network.
sharing.notInstalled: LordOS sessions are not managed by lord-sessiond (see docs/SESSIONS.md): remote desktop is not available.
sharing.openFrom: From another computer on the network, open in a browser:
sharing.remoteHint: Other computers on your local network sign in from a web browser with a username and password of this computer. With your own user they see and use this same screen; with another user, a desktop of their own.
sharing.root.activeWarning: Root can log in over SSH on this computer. Turn it off when you no longer need it.
sharing.root.confirm.addKey: Allow this key to log in as root? Type your password to confirm.
sharing.root.confirm.key: Let root log in over SSH with a public key? Whoever holds a matching private key gets full control of this computer. Type your password to confirm.
sharing.root.confirm.off: Turn root over SSH off? Type your password to confirm.
sharing.root.confirm.password: Let root log in over SSH with a password too? Anyone on the network who learns or guesses it gets full control of this computer. Type your password to confirm.
sharing.root.confirm.removeKey: Remove this key from root's allowed keys? Type your password to confirm.
sharing.root.createHint: To create a key pair, run ssh-keygen -t ed25519 on the computer you'll connect from, and paste or import its .pub file here. The private key never leaves that computer.
sharing.root.footer: Off by default. Root over SSH gives whoever has the key or the password full control of this computer: use it for tests and administration on a network you trust, and turn it off afterwards. Every change asks for your password again.
sharing.root.keyPlaceholder: Paste a public key (ssh-ed25519 AAAA… name@computer)
sharing.root.modeHint.key: Only with one of the public keys below.
sharing.root.modeHint.off: Root never logs in over the network (the default).
sharing.root.modeHint.password: With a key below or root's password: the riskiest choice.
sharing.root.passwordUnset: Root has no password yet: set one to log in with it
sharing.root.title: Advanced: root over SSH
sharing.security: The connection is encrypted (TLS) with a certificate of this computer. 3 failed sign-ins block the address; the root account can never sign in. To use it from the internet, use a VPN.
sharing.sshFingerprint: Host key fingerprint (compare it with the one ssh shows the first time you connect):
sharing.sshFrom: From another computer, run in a terminal:
sharing.sshHint: Other computers open a terminal on this one with an SSH client, using a username and password of this computer. Once on, it stays on after restarting.
sharing.sshHintInstall: Other computers open a terminal on this one with an SSH client, using a username and password of this computer. The SSH server is installed the first time you turn this on (it needs the internet).
sharing.sshNotRunning: Remote login is turned on but the SSH server is not running. Turn it off and on again, or see Logs.
sharing.sshSecurity: Port 22. Passwords travel encrypted. Logging in with a key is safer: copy yours with ssh-copy-id. To use it from the internet, use a VPN.
sharing.sshWhoAdminsHint: Only administrators (the sudo group). Root can never log in.
sharing.sshWhoAllHint: Any user of this computer with a password. Root can never log in.
sharing.stunHint: This computer answers STUN itself, which is enough on the local network. Add a public server only to connect across networks (up to 4, separated by commas).
sharing.turnFooter: Only when neither side can reach the other directly. The relay only sees encrypted video and input; its password stays on this computer, readable only by the system.
sharing.turnFpHint: Empty: the relay’s certificate must be valid for its name. For a relay with its own certificate, paste its SHA-256 fingerprint here.
sharing.videoFooter: Works across the local network and VPNs over UDP, or over TCP port {port} where UDP is blocked. To connect across networks, add a STUN server or a relay below.
sharing.videoHint: The screen, its sound and your input travel encrypted over WebRTC: the only way the remote desktop works.
sharing.whoAllHint: Any user of this computer with a password.
sharing.whoGroupHint: Only users in the lordos-remote group.
sound.unavailable: No connection to the sound server (PipeWire). See docs/SOUND.md.
style.hint: Both styles have the same apps. The change is applied right away, without logging out; open windows come back.
style.title: Desktop style
system.hint: For all users and services (/etc/default/locale). Now: {name}
system.title: System default region
themes.hint: A theme is a React app in themes/<name>. See themes/README.md to make your own.
tz.title: Time zone
updates.hint: LordOS checks the Debian repositories with its own package engine and verifies their signatures. Updates are installed from the Store.
users.autologinHint: When the computer starts, it signs in with this user without the login screen. Off by default.
users.badFull: The full name cannot contain : , or =.
users.badName: The username is lowercase, without spaces or accents (letters, digits, _ and -).
users.deleteConfirm: Delete the account of {name}? Their session will be closed.
users.lastAdmin: This is the only administrator: it cannot be removed.
users.makeAdminHint: Can install software, change the network and manage other users.
users.onlyOwn: Without administrator rights you can only change your own account.
wallpaperImage.loginDone: The login screen will use this picture.
wallpaperImage.name: Your picture
wallpaperImage.hint: PNG or JPEG, up to 64 MB. A copy is kept, so the original can move.
kb.shortcuts.note: Each app adds its own: see its Help article. Plain Ctrl+Q always stays with the app.
osk.title: On-Screen Keyboard
osk.hint: It opens only when you ask for it: its button next to the clock, ❖⌃K, or Show Keyboard here. On the login and lock screens, its button next to the language.
kb.switcher.title: App switcher
kb.switcher.hideMinimized: Leave out apps with every window minimized
kb.switcher.numbers: Number the apps (press 1 to 9 to go to one)
kb.switcher.hint: While it is open: Tab moves, Z or the key under Esc moves through the app's windows, and letting go switches.
kb.switcher.hintOverview: In Lord Classic, when ❖ Tab opens the switcher, the Overview moves to ❖ W.
kb.switcher.excludedHint: Open apps, and any you have left out. Turn one off and it never shows in the switcher.
dock.desktops.title: Desktops
dock.desktops.hint: Each desktop has its own windows. A removed desktop's windows move to the one beside it. Use the Overview to see them all.
dock.desktops.arrows: Use Ctrl + arrow keys for Desktops
dock.desktops.arrowsHint: Ctrl+Up opens the Overview, Ctrl+Left and Right switch desktops, Ctrl+Down shows the windows of the app in front.
dock.desktops.namesHint: Leave a name empty to use the default. In the Overview, double-click a desktop's name to rename it, or drag it along the strip to change the order.
kb.desktopArrows.title: Desktops
kb.desktopArrows.label: Use Ctrl + arrow keys for Desktops
kb.desktopArrows.hint: Ctrl+Up opens the Overview, Ctrl+Left and Right switch desktops, Ctrl+Down shows the windows of the app. Turn this off to keep these keys for moving by word in apps; Super+Ctrl+Left and Right still switch desktops.
motion.title: Moving wallpapers
motion.hint: Downloaded when you choose one. They pause when the desktop is hidden, in full screen, when you step away, and on low battery.
motion.needsGpu: Moving wallpapers need a compatible GPU.
motion.problem.tooLong: The video lasts more than 10 seconds.
motion.problem.format: This GPU can't decode that video format.
motion.problem.unreadable: That file can't be read as a video.
motion.loginDone: The login screen will use this video.
motion.loginReset: The login screen is back to its default video.
sharing.inUseBy: In use by {app}. Remote desktop can’t sign in to this session until it ends.
lang.preferredHint: The first language is used by LordOS and its apps (the login screen keeps its own, chosen there). When a text isn’t translated, the next ones are used, in order.
lang.notYetHint: LordOS isn’t translated into {name} yet. You can already use its date and number formats with Region below, and ask for the language at github.com/lordbasex/LordOS/issues.
